Weighted power (generalised) mean of `values` in [0,1].

        p != 0:  ( Σ wᵢ · sᵢ^p )^(1/p)
        p == 0:  exp( Σ wᵢ · ln sᵢ )      (geometric mean, the limit p→0)

    weak (or zero) factor drags the result down hard but cannot collapse the
    whole thing to zero. Weights are renormalised defensively to sum to 1.

schedules.directive: # GIGA Programme — Master File
*This file is to the operator what the slice feeder is to orchestrator-v3: the programme, the
sequencing, and the single progress table. Every session reads this FIRST, works exactly one
brief, and updates the table before closing. One source of truth; briefs never duplicate it.*
## The rule (inherited from the orchestrator, applies to every session)
No output is trusted until it survives contact with reality. Every session must leave a
**durable artefact** — a deployed config, a script, a document in this folder, or a working
integration. Insight that lives only in chat produced no leverage. Claims about the operator's
behaviour are hypotheses until his own data or explicit confirmation backs them.
## Operator context — read `CONTEXT.md` (canonical), not this block
Operator identity, situation, active state, and **the standing-decision registry** live in
`CONTEXT.md` — the single home of settled doctrine since the 18 Jul entropy merge. This
file no longer restates any of it.
**Existing assets to reuse, not reinvent** (programme mechanics, so kept here): the
(Mode A/B/C reviews, the cost-audit brief), the v3 planning corpus
(`~/Documents/agentic-orchestrator/docs/planning/`, esp. 18 & 19), and the owned corpus
(`corpus/` — MANIFEST.md holds canon and counting rules; the 26 Jul local unified-memory
authority contains 532,274 observations across both Discord accounts, Telegram, full two-sided
Instagram, Claude and both ChatGPT accounts, with 28 evidence-linked Tier-3 hypotheses).
**On characterisation:** any behavioural claim about the operator must be corpus-derived or
explicitly confirmed — never asserted from chat impressions. `CONTEXT.md` and `memory/` are
the sanctioned, evidence-backed homes of who he is; the digital twin derives from the corpus
per its five-stage roadmap (memory entry `2026-07-18-bot-maturation-roadmap`).
## The programme workstreams — one session each, in this order
| # | Session | Deliverables | Status | Session log |

| 01 | Unified operator charter | one charter → three deployments (Claude preferences, ChatGPT custom instructions, v3 operator-model file) + test protocol | DONE (18 Jul, operator-closed) — v1.1 live on all three surfaces; standing revert clause if he becomes unsatisfied; Session 04 still reviews the week | `SESSION_LOGS/01_log.md` |

| 02 | Memory & standing context | standing-context doc; deployed to Claude + ChatGPT memory; update cadence; recitation verification | DONE (18 Jul) — CONTEXT v1.0 live on Claude (PASS), ChatGPT (PASS qualified — dates omitted; snapshot staleness noted), bot (PASS, live-read) | `SESSION_LOGS/02_log.md` |
| 03 | Life infrastructure | Gmail + Calendar connected read-only; scheduled morning brief working; injection posture applied; texts-tier scoped | NOT STARTED | — |

| 04 | Prompt corpus & reasoning retrospective | chat exports landed as corpus; retrospective evaluator; first retrospective report with pattern findings + discard rate | IN PROGRESS (26 Jul) — both Discord accounts, both ChatGPT accounts, Claude, native Telegram and full two-sided Instagram are unified into a 532,274-observation three-tier local evidence database; the teen-account developmental pass, corrected Sneg record, longitudinal signals and 28 evidence-linked Tier-3 hypotheses are complete; validation-selected speech and reasoning-steering LoRAs were trained and locked-test/synthetic evaluated—the speech model remains unpromoted and the reasoning model failed as a thinking clone; operator calibration/discard-rate and blind speech review remain | `SESSION_LOGS/04_log.md` |

| 05 | Calibration & prompt bank | personal prediction ledger + scoring script; prompt-pattern bank harvested from proven briefs; review cadence | IN PROGRESS (20 Jul) — autonomous SQLite forecast→evidence→calibration loop integrated into daily Jarvis; no manual predictions; prompt bank + review cadence remain | `SESSION_LOGS/05_log.md` |

| 06 | The second memory (Jarvis) | `memory/` deepened: 20+ seeded entries, capture habit wired, daily sweep scheduled, synthesis test passed | DONE (18 Jul; daily capture amended 19 Jul) — bot + skill + folder-chat mesh; Cowork + Codex harvested daily at 06:06 ICT; INGEST + recency law; Claude→GPT fallback; synthesis test passed | `SESSION_LOGS/06_log.md` |

| 07 | Virtual-twin control plane | three-depth architecture maps; target model; transition roadmap; trust kernel; transactional capture; memory/decision/evaluation/agency promotion gates | IN PROGRESS (29 Jul) — P0/P1 pass; P2 Telegram/daily paths deployed, first natural daily run + fault injection remain; relationship-event graph designed; evidence-backed SkillTree registry, draft-only external-proof compiler, read-only operator-status contract and hashed no-authority adapter registry pass; pinned ECC portable extraction complete; deterministic execution-boundary architecture selected but not deployed, with Telegram proposed as the first later enforcement slice; append-only artefact revisions and operator-authorized lineage reconciliation implemented; provider-neutral scientific evidence acquisition, deterministic screening and a six-stage hash-bound review funnel are live and A0-only; the refined skin campaign maps 6,108 records and all 37 questions reproducibly into 4,144 groups, with 2,144 missing-abstract retrievals programmatically queued, while five duplicate decisions, exclusion audit, human eligibility, saturation, full-text extraction/appraisal and ranking remain explicitly blocked; Market Aligner remains independent | `SESSION_LOGS/07_log.md` |
**Why this order:** 01 defines the voice everything else speaks in; 02 gives every surface the
same brain; 03 is independent and high-value (do it early for daily payoff); 04 needs exports
and benefits from 01/02 being live (cleaner data); 05 wants 04's corpus for its first scoring.
**06 is the keystone and can run any time** — its skeleton is already live (`memory/` with
protocol, index, seed entries; any session pointed at this folder acts as librarian per the
protocol). Sessions 02 and 03 should treat the memory as their substrate: the context doc is
its identity tier, the morning brief is its reminder surface — one store, several surfaces.
**07 is the integration stage, not a replacement for 01–06.** It turns their evidence and
services into a provider-neutral, measurable virtual-twin control plane. It consumes domain
events through adapters; it does not physically absorb or interrupt Market Aligner.

# Session 01 — The Unified Operator Charter
*Read `00_MASTER.md` first. Mission: Artiom's orchestrator has a constitution with machine
checks; his Claude has two lines of preferences; his ChatGPT has none. Produce ONE operator
charter and deploy it to all three surfaces. This is the highest-leverage evening in the
programme — it defines the voice every later session speaks in.*
## Deliverables (all four, in this folder + deployed)
1. `CHARTER.md` — the canonical document. **Policies, not constants** (no "respond in N
characters" cargo cult): default register, depth rule, challenge mandate, evidence
2. `deploy/claude_preferences.txt` — condensed for Claude's personal-preferences field, and
WALK HIM THROUGH pasting it (Settings → Profile → preferences).
3. `deploy/chatgpt_custom_instructions.txt` — the two-box format (about-me / how-to-respond),
4. `deploy/v3_operator_model.md` — the machine-readable variant staged for orchestrator-v3's
future operator-model capability (do NOT touch the orchestrator repos; stage it here).
1. **Start from DATA, not impressions — there is deliberately no personal profile in
00_MASTER.** Your two evidence sources: the extracted corpus (`corpus/raw/prompts_*.jsonl`,
545 hand-authored prompts — mine it for how he actually writes, what he asks for, what he
corrects) and the interview below. Any behavioural claim you form must cite corpus
evidence or his explicit answer; characterisation without evidence is the failure mode
this whole programme exists to kill.
2. **Interview him — deep, not a form.** Cover at least: how hard should pushback be, and on
what topics is it unwelcome; when does he want one-line answers vs essays; what should
NEVER be assumed; which past AI responses does he remember as excellent or terrible, and
why (get 2–3 concrete examples each — they're worth more than any abstraction); how should
uncertainty be expressed; what standing goals should shape every answer (career clock).
3. **Draft the charter with him in the loop** — each clause traceable to either an observed
pattern or his explicit answer. Include a "challenge mandate" section: the evidence says he
ratifies good disagreement; encode the licence AND its limits.
4. **Deploy all three variants**, then run the **test protocol**: take 3 real prompts from his
recent usage, run them under old and new configuration, have him judge blind which
response serves him better. The charter ships only if it wins.
5. Set a revision trigger: the charter is versioned here; Session 04's retrospectives feed
amendments to it (note the seam in your log).
`CHARTER.md` exists and is deployed to both live surfaces; the A/B test is run and recorded;
the v3 variant is staged; `SESSION_LOGS/01_log.md` written; master table updated.

## Mandatory skill routing for giga-user
- Apply the global `skill-router` gate to every substantive request in this project. Evaluate the complete installed catalog and use every genuinely matching skill.
- `skill-creator`, `skill-installer`, and `find-skills` remain mandatory for skill lifecycle work; never edit or install a skill ad hoc.

- For the career pipeline: route scraping/crawling to `scrapling-official`; deterministic application flows to `playwright`; and unsupported interactive forms to `browser-use`. Apply security skills only when their own explicit trigger conditions are satisfied.
- Invoke `account-research` only after opportunity assessment passes, then use it for employer, team, decision-maker, product, hiring-signal, and public leverage research with source attribution.
- Route UK CV and cover-letter construction through `resume-cover-letter`, then `humanizer`, only after the evidence ledger and eligibility validation have fixed the truthful claims.
- Preserve the profiler/evidence ledger as the source of truth. No skill may invent qualifications, experience, preferences, work rights, or application answers.

- Route SkillTree audits, capability-status questions, gap prioritisation, and node implementation through `skilltree-operator`. The immutable public export is taxonomy evidence only; require the generated giga-user implementation registry before claiming a node is deployed.

(545-prompt extraction, Jun–Jul 2026), [I‑n] = interview answer n (16 Jul 2026).*

spelling. No emojis, no filler, no cheerleading. [I‑8, C: median hand-typed prompt 120 chars]
## 2. Depth — short is king
Most generated text goes unread; compression is respect. One-line answers are complete answers.
Go deep only for vision, architecture, or course-correction — and when unsure which, **write
short**. Never pad, never restate the question, never summarise what he just said. [I‑2]
Disagreement is a service. When the assistant believes he is wrong, it challenges **before**
complying, with evidence, at full strength — his hardest engagement follows pushback, and
superior counter-proposals get adopted ("your 8-field register is strictly better than my 3").
Limits: the standing-decision registry (CONTEXT.md — the single home of settled doctrine) is
not relitigated without new evidence; once he overrules with reasons, execute without
sulking. [I‑1, C: 16 Jul; registry merge 18 Jul]

circular hash dependency in which compiling either file immediately invalidates the other.

It must not mean placing every conversation into a context window or baking mutable life facts
into model weights. It means the twin can address the entire authorised evidence corpus and
compile the right bounded packet for the present situation.

- **Working memory:** current goals, plans, active constraints and recent context.
- **Behavioural model:** preferences, reasoning tendencies, habits and uncertainty—not facts.
- **Voice model:** mode-conditioned language behaviour—not biography.

# Relationship event graph: four-friend pilot
Build an **event-sourced temporal knowledge graph**, not a neural network as the source of
truth. A future embedding model or temporal graph neural network may consume the graph, but
neither may become the authority for who said what or when.

context, meetings and topic segments where explicitly recoverable.
3. **Interpretation:** speech acts, disclosure, support, humour, hierarchy, conflict, repair,
warmth and relationship-state estimates, each probabilistic and linked to evidence.

# Deterministic execution boundary — architecture decision
*Design only · 2026-07-22 · not deployed · grants no new authority*
GIGA should enforce deterministic-first execution through a **small in-process policy kernel**, a
single **canonical capability registry**, and a **static bypass audit** over every declared official
It should not begin with a daemon, MCP server, prompt rule, database migration or operating-system
sandbox. Those mechanisms either add operational surface or fail to express the decisive rule:
> For an official GIGA operation, deterministic code decides eligibility, evidence, authority and
> completion. A model may generate a typed proposal only when the registry explicitly permits it.
> The model cannot grant authority, claim completion or choose to bypass the deterministic path.
This is the smallest architecture that can turn the current convention into a testable guarantee.
The guarantee is intentionally bounded to **registered official execution surfaces**. It cannot
prevent the repository owner from running arbitrary Python or replacing the local database.
## Why this is now the right slice
The portable ECC extraction is complete and its freeze permits design review. Current source
inspection shows that GIGA already has most of the required primitives:
- deterministic context compilation in `twin_core/context_compiler.py`;
- no-tool Claude/Codex proposal generation in `twin_core/provider_adapters.py`;
- deterministic proposal validation and commit in `twin_core/memory_proposals.py`;
- append-only events, attempts and receipts in `twin_core/store.py`;
- read-only adapter evidence and operator-status compilers;
- a tested schema-v3 candidate whose database concerns are separate from execution routing.
What is missing is a single mandatory decision point. Today:
- Telegram and daily memory use the safe proposal lifecycle, but call it by convention;
- the daily prediction worker invokes providers through a second direct implementation;
- Jarvis starts the daily process directly;
- standalone scripts can perform writes, subprocesses or network calls without consulting one
- the evidence registry describes adapters but deliberately grants no execution authority;
- no check proves that all official entry points pass through the same decision boundary.

Every governed operation enters the kernel as a closed, versioned request. The minimum fields are:

Unknown fields fail validation. Missing evidence remains unknown; it never silently becomes an
The existing adapter-evidence registry remains a **read-only evidence surface**. Execution policy
must be a separate registry so evidence cannot accidentally become authority. Each capability entry

Registry loading must be deterministic, root-contained and fail closed on duplicates, path escape,

The kernel returns one of four closed decisions:
1. `deterministic` — execute the registered deterministic handler;
2. `proposal-only` — a no-tool model may return the registered typed proposal;
3. `replay` — return a matching committed receipt without new work or tokens;
4. `refuse` — evidence, freshness, authority, budget or capability registration is insufficient.
A decision is bound to request hash, registry hash, evidence hashes and expiry. The first
implementation need not persist a separate transferable “permit”; keeping decision and execution
in one process avoids a time-of-check/time-of-use token that can be replayed by another process.
If a later distributed design needs permits, they require nonce, expiry, single-use consumption
“Deterministic first” does **not** mean pretending deterministic code can write a good summary or
interpret ambiguous language. It means deterministic code owns routing and truth:
- it tries replay and deterministic resolution before spending tokens;
- it invokes a model only for a registry-declared judgement or generation gap;
- model input is bounded and provider-neutral;
- model tools and write authority remain absent;
- model output is always a proposal with a strict schema;
- deterministic code validates path, evidence, policy, semantics and current-state preconditions;
- only a deterministic transition can produce a committed receipt;
- a provider label or confident sentence is never success evidence.
Identical receipted input returns the receipt and consumes no new model tokens. Deterministic
fixtures must prove zero provider calls, not merely a preferred ordering.
The kernel does not expand the current A0–AX policy. It makes the ceiling executable:
- A0/A1 read and draft operations may run when registered;
- A2 produces a complete version-bound artifact and waits for an explicit human receipt;
- A3/A4 remain unavailable until each capability has its own rollback, live evidence and promotion
- AX refuses execution regardless of model confidence;
- the model cannot create, widen or approve an authority record;
- an approval is bound to the exact artifact/request hash; edits invalidate it.

## Versioning, schema v2/v3 and entropy
The execution contract, capability registry and TwinStore database are different version domains.
- This design does not require TwinStore schema v3. Existing events, attempts and receipts are
enough for the first shadow and Telegram slices.
- A registry `v1` or request `v1` does not imply database schema v1, v2 or v3.
- Schema v3 should advance only for its own integrity/migration benefits under
`architecture/09_SCHEMA_V3_READINESS.md`, never as a hidden prerequisite of routing.
- If a future receipt needs semantically new durable fields that cannot be represented truthfully
in existing JSON details, that is a separate, explicit migration decision.
Entropy is controlled by having one canonical registry and generating every derived surface from
- two active registry versions for one process;

### Writer topology and completion inbox
The controller is the only authoritative database writer. Workers never update state, leases,
budgets or certificates directly. They atomically publish an attempt-specific completion or
heartbeat envelope to a certified local inbox/CAS location and notify the controller. The
controller verifies controller generation, attempt token, operation identity, artifact hashes,
authority and current state before committing one settlement transaction. After takeover, an old
worker envelope can be retained as untrusted recovery evidence, but only a typed reconciliation
under the new generation may adopt it. Inbox capacity is reserved before admission and completion
envelopes are never dropped. This avoids SQLite writer contention and makes fencing enforceable at
one boundary without trusting worker code. Authoritative transactions stay short; no model,
subprocess, filesystem scan or network call executes while a database transaction is open.

## Residual risks that cannot honestly be designed away
| Residual risk | Why it remains | Required containment |

| Provider accepted a request but no response was captured | Most providers do not expose a complete exactly-once transaction with local state | Preserve `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`; reconcile by provider idempotency/status when available, otherwise make any second call explicit and measured |

| A semantic reviewer misses a real defect | Model judgement is probabilistic and tests/specifications can also be incomplete | Independent roles, deterministic gates, negative controls, blinded parity, coverage ledger and full release review; never claim proof of semantic correctness |

| Scope reviewer misses part of operator intent | Natural-language intent is not mechanically complete | Immutable intent receipt, omission fixtures, explicit scope certificate and amendment path; uncertainty/refusal is preferable to silent narrowing |

| Dynamic runtime behaviour defeats static impact proof | Reflection, generated code and external systems are not fully statically knowable | Mark uncertainty and force full review/fresh execution; never infer delta safety from absence of an edge |

| Hardware/filesystem loses already acknowledged durable bytes | Local durability primitives reduce but cannot eliminate device/firmware failure | Generation-bound backups, restore drills, integrity checks and no false claim of zero data-loss probability |

| Provider/model behaviour changes without a useful immutable revision | External model infrastructure can drift | Versioned route policy, recurring eval receipts and immediate frontier/full-review fallback when identity or parity is uncertain |
These are controlled failure states, not waived requirements. The factory must report which one it
encountered instead of manufacturing deterministic certainty.

### Phase 0 — preserve the baseline
1. Settle the separately owned dirty isolation work and record the clean Gigabyte v3 commit.
2. Export the current JAA scorecard and pin its task-log hash.
3. Freeze a production epoch with the active E1–E6 settings.
4. Build a replay set from accepted, rejected, timed-out, tool-capped, stale-checkpoint and semantic
rejection episodes. Do not spend live JAA tokens to discover basic regressions.
### Phase 1 — remove model calls the controller does not need
1. Add the structured finding ledger without changing scheduling.
2. Build a shadow manifest-to-workflow compiler.
3. Compare its steps with the existing task manager on the replay set.
4. Activate only for complete, unambiguous contracts; retain planner fallback.
This is the safest first code change because it does not alter tests, judging or merge gates.
### Phase 2 — make semantic assurance incremental
1. Build the exact impact/dependency package and certificate-composition schema.
2. Run delta and full judges side-by-side in shadow mode.
3. Inject completeness failures and known JAA findings.
4. Activate only after material-finding parity; retain automatic full-review escalation.
This is the largest direct token opportunity and therefore deserves the strongest activation gate.
### Phase 3 — durable operation graph
1. Represent the existing compiled workflow as durable nodes without changing execution.
2. Persist completed model-call outputs and context packages under exact invocation identities.
3. Prove crash-after-provider-return resumes without a second provider call.
4. Generalise reuse node by node; keep side effects non-reusable by default.

1. Benchmark model routes per role and risk class using ECC-style pinned evaluation records.
2. Activate a cascade for the lowest-risk role first.
3. Add two-lane builder/tester execution only for disjoint ownership.
4. Measure the combined profile against both historical and current baselines.

V3 is not slow because assurance is inherently incompatible with speed. It is slow because its
assurance is repeatedly wrapped in expensive, general-purpose model turns and repeatedly applied
to unchanged work while the factory itself keeps moving.
The right design is **host-deterministic by default, model-semantic only where necessary,
incrementally certified during development, and fully certified at release**. That preserves what

# Orchestrator v2/v3 versus native Codex autonomy
Status: evidence-backed preliminary comparison; controlled head-to-head benchmark not yet run
Measurement cutoff: 25 July 2026, 17:48 UTC for the native Codex session; approximately
17:44 UTC for the Gigabyte supervisor snapshot
Native Codex currently beats v3 at **continuity economics**: one agent retains ownership of a
changing problem, plans and replans inside the same trajectory, uses tools directly, compacts its
own context, and crosses many implementation/test/repair steps without buying a new
planner-builder-tester-judge conversation for each step. [inference, confidence 0.96]
V3 beats native Codex at **defensibility**: exact state, revision-bound receipts, deterministic
host assurance, independent semantic judgement, isolated worktrees, explicit retries, STOP,
certificates and replayable operational decisions. [verified, confidence 0.99]
- native Codex is fast and adaptive, but its trajectory is not a deterministic workflow
- v3 is highly auditable, but it repeatedly decomposes one cognitive job into costly role
transitions and repeatedly assures work that has not materially changed;
- the current thin Codex/Sonnet/Fable supervisor demonstrates unattended continuity, but it is
an external control script around Codex rather than proof that v3 has acquired that capability.
The design target should therefore be:
> **Codex-like continuous cognition inside a thin v3 deterministic perimeter.**
The deterministic layer should own identity, authority, isolation, budgets, durable checkpoints,
side effects, evidence and certification. A persistent work capsule should own the internal
plan→edit→test→diagnose→repair loop. The factory should not represent every thought or microstep as
a separately planned and judged task. [architectural conclusion, confidence 0.94]
This report does **not** claim that native Codex is token-cheap. The measured app session is
enormous. Its advantage is that 98.53% of recorded input was cache-served and that the same
trajectory retained operational ownership; it did not eliminate context, it made context

## Why native Codex currently feels more autonomous
### 1. It has one cognitive owner
Codex does not normally purchase a separate planner verdict before every edit, a separate tester
interpretation after every edit, and a separate planner turn after every finding. One loop can
inspect, act, observe and revise until the task is settled.
V3’s role separation is useful for independence, but it incorrectly applies independence to
micro-coordination as well as terminal assurance. The result is a handoff tax on ordinary thought.
### 2. It treats tool observations as continuation, not as new work
A failed test becomes the next observation in the same trajectory. In v3 it can become a failed
task result, transition, fingerprint, requeue, planner input, new worktree attempt, host gate and
new judge context. The latter is more defensible, but much more expensive.
### 3. It caches a stable prefix
Native Codex’s 98.53% cached-input ratio shows that a large, stable context prefix can be reused
across thousands of tool interactions. V3 deliberately uses ephemeral role calls for contamination
control, but loses the economic benefit of a persistent working set.
The right response is not one immortal, unbounded chat. It is a bounded persistent **work capsule**
whose immutable contract and context prefix are stable until the component closes.
The measured native session compacted 81 times without requiring an external planner to
reconstruct the work. V3’s summaries, task results and receipts are stronger evidence, but they are
also repeatedly expanded back into model-readable prose.
### 5. Native orchestration is mostly implicit
Codex’s orchestration code is a platform capability and is not part of this repository’s
maintenance surface. V3 must build, test and certify every scheduler, schema, ledger, cache,
checkpoint and gate it owns. Comparing only runtime tokens hides this construction tax.
## Where v3 is genuinely superior
The answer is not to abandon v3 and use a naked Codex session:
1. A Codex trajectory records what happened; v3 can prove which exact product closure was
2. Native resume does not by itself prove exactly-once durable consumption of a provider result
3. Native tool success is not automatically a component certificate with dependency, runtime,
4. Native self-review is not independent review.
5. A long autonomous session can drift, overfit to its own previous reasoning, silently weaken
tests or retain contaminated context. V3 has explicit gates against these classes.
6. V3 can make model/provider choice replaceable while retaining one workflow truth.
These are commercially material advantages. The error is not building them; it is placing them
inside the inner cognitive loop rather than around its meaningful boundaries.
## Precise diagnosis of the gap
The current gap is not one bug. It is a difference in **unit of orchestration**:
-> inspect -> plan -> edit -> test -> diagnose -> repair -> finish
-> schedule -> package context -> call model -> parse -> settle -> assure
-> schedule another role action -> package context again -> call model again
-> deterministic admission and immutable contract
-> durable checkpoints and host gates at material state changes
-> independent delta review at capsule boundary
-> full independent review at release
V3 should determinise **authority and evidence**, not attempt to determinise every intermediate
reasoning step. [architectural conclusion, confidence 0.96]

# The Second Memory — Librarian Protocol
*Any AI session pointed at this folder acts as the librarian of Artiom's second memory. The
pattern is inherited from his own proven systems (orchestrator KB, Cowork memory): one entry
per file, frontmatter, an always-loaded index, entries never edited destructively — superseded
entries are amended with a pointer, so the memory has history like an event log.*
## The three duties (every interaction, in order)
1. **FILE** — when he throws an idea/fact/decision/reminder: classify it, write
`entries/<date>-<slug>.md` with frontmatter, link related entries `[[like-this]]`, update
`INDEX.md` (one line per entry — the index is what future sessions load first).
2. **COLLIDE** — filing is never passive. Check the new entry against the index: does it
contradict, extend, duplicate, or unlock an existing entry? Say so out loud — the
connections he hasn't made are the entire point ("meaningful thinking I haven't come up
with yet" lives here, not in the filing).
3. **REMIND** — check `type: reminder` entries whose trigger matches the current conversation
context or date, and surface them unprompted. A reminder surfaced twice without action gets
flagged for decision (act / reschedule / archive), never silently repeated forever.
type: idea | decision | fact | reminder | question
trigger: (reminders only) a date, or "when discussing <topic>"
status: active | superseded-by [[entry]] | archived
The entry. One thought per file. Links to related entries [[by-slug]].
For decisions: the rationale and rejected alternatives (traceability — his C3 rule).
- **One thought per entry; the index is sacred** (regenerate its line on every write).
- **Never delete** — archive or supersede with a pointer (history is data).
- **No secrets** — no credentials, tokens, or data he wouldn't want in plaintext.
- **Challenge is a duty**: if a new idea contradicts a standing `decision` entry, say so
before filing — he ratifies good pushback; silent contradiction is corruption.
- **The weekly sweep** (scheduled or manual): resurface due reminders; hunt one non-obvious
connection between a recent entry and a dormant one; propose archiving stale actives;

# The Second Memory — Librarian Protocol
*Any AI session pointed at this folder acts as the librarian of Artiom's second memory. The
pattern is inherited from his own proven systems (orchestrator KB, Cowork memory): one entry
per file, frontmatter, an always-loaded index, entries never edited destructively — superseded
entries are amended with a pointer, so the memory has history like an event log.*
## The three duties (every interaction, in order)
1. **FILE** — when he throws an idea/fact/decision/reminder: classify it, write
`entries/<date>-<slug>.md` with frontmatter, link related entries `[[like-this]]`, update
`INDEX.md` (one line per entry — the index is what future sessions load first).
2. **COLLIDE** — filing is never passive. Check the new entry against the index: does it
contradict, extend, duplicate, or unlock an existing entry? Say so out loud — the
connections he hasn't made are the entire point ("meaningful thinking I haven't come up
with yet" lives here, not in the filing).
3. **REMIND** — check `type: reminder` entries whose trigger matches the current conversation
context or date, and surface them unprompted. A reminder surfaced twice without action gets
flagged for decision (act / reschedule / archive), never silently repeated forever.
type: idea | decision | fact | reminder | question
trigger: (reminders only) a date, or "when discussing <topic>"
status: active | superseded-by [[entry]] | archived
The entry. One thought per file. Links to related entries [[by-slug]].
For decisions: the rationale and rejected alternatives (traceability — his C3 rule).
- **One thought per entry; the index is sacred** (regenerate its line on every write).
- **Never delete** — archive or supersede with a pointer (history is data).
- **No secrets** — no credentials, tokens, or data he wouldn't want in plaintext.
- **Challenge is a duty**: if a new idea contradicts a standing `decision` entry, say so
before filing — he ratifies good pushback; silent contradiction is corruption.
- **The weekly sweep** (scheduled or manual): resurface due reminders; hunt one non-obvious
connection between a recent entry and a dormant one; propose archiving stale actives;

The memory lives in exactly one place: the **`memory/` directory of the giga-user folder**
(`/Users/admin/Documents/giga-user/memory/` — in sandboxed shells it may be mounted under a
different root; resolve the giga-user folder first). Layout: `INDEX.md` (always read first),
`MEMORY_PROTOCOL.md` (the full contract — read it before your first write in a session),
If this folder is not reachable from the current session, **request folder access or refuse
loudly**. Never file into a local improvisation, a different memory system, or plain chat
text — a second store silently forks the memory and corrupts the single-source-of-truth
## The three duties (every invocation, in order)
1. **FILE** — classify the thought (`idea | decision | fact | reminder | question`), write
`entries/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` with the frontmatter format defined in
`MEMORY_PROTOCOL.md`, link related entries `[[by-slug]]`, and regenerate that entry's
line in `INDEX.md`. One thought per file — split compound thoughts.
2. **COLLIDE** — filing is never passive. Check the new entry against the index: does it
contradict, extend, duplicate, or unlock an existing entry? Say so out loud. The
connections he hasn't made himself are the entire point of this memory. If a new thought
contradicts a standing `decision` entry, challenge before filing — silent contradiction
3. **REMIND** — scan `type: reminder` entries whose trigger (a date, or "when discussing
<topic>") matches the current conversation, and surface them unprompted. A reminder
surfaced twice without action gets flagged for a decision: act, reschedule, or archive.
## Laws (from the protocol — it is canonical if this summary ever drifts)
- Never delete; supersede or archive with a pointer. History is data.
- No secrets: no credentials, tokens, or anything he wouldn't keep in plaintext.
- Retrieval questions ("what did I say about…") answer from entries, cited by slug.
- The weekly sweep, when asked: resurface due reminders; find one non-obvious connection
between a recent entry and a dormant one; propose archiving stale actives; ≤10 lines.
- Use only file operations and shell — no environment-specific tools — so this skill
behaves identically in Cowork, Claude Code, and orchestrator-v3.

The registry is derived from the immutable public export plus the repository-owned evidence map.
| Status | Deterministic meaning |
| `implemented` | Every required path in an explicit evidence declaration exists. |
| `partial` | At least one, but not every, required path exists, or the declaration explicitly marks the node partial. |
| `available` | A matching installed/deployed skill can help, but no complete giga-user workflow is evidenced. |
| `external` | An explicit declaration points to a separate canonical system that owns the capability. |
| `blocked` | An explicit declaration records a blocker and no complete local implementation exists. |
| `documented` | The public export describes the node, but none of the stronger states is proven. |
Precedence is `implemented`, `external`, `partial`, `blocked`, `available`, `documented`.

Local evidence declarations use exact repository-relative paths. Directories must exist and contain at least one non-hidden entry. Globs are forbidden. `external` declarations may additionally use exact absolute `external_evidence` paths; these prove a live seam but never count as local implementation. Generated registry files never count as implementation evidence.

An installed skill is availability evidence only. It becomes implementation evidence after a real workflow consumes it, produces durable output, and its acceptance contract is recorded in the evidence map.

# ECC extraction boundary and deferred deterministic enforcement
## Deferred until extraction is complete
Repository-wide deterministic enforcement is necessary if “deterministic first” is to become a
guarantee rather than a convention. It is deliberately deferred until the useful ECC extraction
The later enforcement slice should require every official execution path to:
1. resolve a registered deterministic adapter before considering an LLM;
2. validate current evidence, freshness and authority;
3. treat model output as a proposal rather than verified evidence;
4. refuse unavailable or unauthorised work instead of bypassing the registry;
5. emit a deterministic receipt for every accepted transition;
6. fail CI when an official entry point bypasses the execution gate.
Until the extraction-complete decision is recorded:
- do not rewire all giga-user CLIs, scheduled jobs, Jarvis or external adapters;
- do not introduce a global execution gateway;
- do not claim the current adapter registry universally enforces deterministic routing;
- stage portable ECC findings only under `ecc-integration/`;
- allow only validation and documentation changes needed to prove the extraction itself.

candidate staged in this folder is safe to keep isolated. **ECC is not safe to install wholesale

The JavaScript/Python security guidance catalog contained no general Node CLI or desktop-Python
reference specific to this stack, so this review used repository trust boundaries, upstream tests,
negative fixtures, static inspection and dependency evidence. Rust was reviewed separately through
Cargo tests/clippy and upstream alpha declarations.
### SEC-01 — Do not import auto-update or the global installer
**Impact:** a compromised or wrongly selected local ECC tree could execute its own installer and
`scripts/auto-update.js:124-153` calls a repository trusted when its `package.json` merely uses one
of two expected names and the install script exists; `scripts/auto-update.js:250-267` then fetches,
pulls, and executes that script. This is stronger than no check and the path-safety suite is good,
but package name is not source identity or commit attestation. The installer also intentionally
Decision: reject runtime import. Preserve only the read-only plan/apply/state/rollback architecture,
with commit hashes and explicit promotion.
### SEC-02 — The legacy capability dashboard is not loopback-bound explicitly
`scripts/dashboard-web.js:789-803` exposes agents, skills, commands, rules, MCP metadata and hooks
without authentication and calls `server.listen(PORT)` without a host. The newer control-pane and
plan-canvas servers explicitly use `127.0.0.1` and Host/Origin checks; this older dashboard does not.
Decision: do not import it. Any future UI must bind `127.0.0.1`, validate Host and Origin, default to
read-only, and require a separate authorization boundary for mutations.
### SEC-03 — Passing aggregate coverage hides untested executable entry points
The Node 24 coverage run passed the configured thresholds at 89.14% statements, 79.70% branches,
93.91% functions and 89.14% lines. However, `scripts/orchestrate-worktrees.js` and
`scripts/hooks/cursor-session-env.js` reported 0% coverage, while several update/install/coordination
paths were materially below the aggregate. Aggregate green therefore does not certify every import
Decision: any ported executable needs its own positive, negative, path-escape and rollback tests.
### SEC-04 — Codex support is instruction-backed, not enforcement parity
ECC's own adapter matrix describes Codex as instruction-backed. Claude/OpenCode hook behavior cannot
be treated as a runtime security boundary in Codex.
Decision: import policy as declarations and tests only; never claim a hook control is deployed until
the target harness produces enforcement evidence.
## Low priority / evidence gaps
### SEC-05 — Registry advisory lookup was unavailable
`npm audit --ignore-scripts --json` failed twice because the npm bulk-advisory request returned an
endpoint/network error. This is not evidence of a vulnerability or of a clean dependency set.
`npm audit signatures` did succeed: all 210 packages had verified registry signatures and 24 had
verified attestations. The repository's own supply-chain IOC scan also passed.
Decision: dependency-bearing runtime promotion remains blocked until an advisory scan succeeds (npm,
OSV, or equivalent) against the pinned lockfile.
### SEC-06 — ECC2 is explicitly alpha
`ecc2/README.md:1-5`, `28-35`, and `80-99` calls the control plane alpha, incomplete, and not GA.
Decision: comparative reference only. Do not merge it with orchestrator-v3.

# Operational assurance contract (staged, not deployed)
## Evidence before a readiness claim
A readiness assessment names the exact release surface and records, when applicable:
- build, type, lint and test results;
- deterministic security and secret checks;
- migration, retry, idempotency and recovery evidence;
- startup, health, observability and incident-owner paths;
- critical user-path or end-to-end evidence;
- evidence checked and evidence still missing.
Checks are `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable` or `not-applicable` with source and timestamp. Missing
evidence is never converted to a passing score.
- Any unresolved sensitive authorization, exposed secret, unsafe destructive migration,
non-idempotent high-impact webhook or missing high-impact rollback caps readiness below release.
- Non-green CI or an untested launch-critical path caps readiness below an unconditional “ready.”
- A numeric score prioritises work; it does not override a failed cap.

# Independent-product integration boundary (staged, not deployed)
An external product can contribute useful workflows without being absorbed into giga-user.
- a public/local path that works without private credentials;
- a gated path for live account data or actions;
- ownership, billing and support responsibilities;
- sanitized fixtures and public documentation;
- evaluation, risk and authority gates;
- receipts proving any completed external action.
Private keys, account state and proprietary strategy remain outside public workflows and prompts.
Patterns learned from real usage may return only as sanitized examples, tests or generic contracts.
An integration does not transfer product ownership, source-of-truth status or action authority.

Your four-part split is the right shape. One refinement changes how they connect: **the LLM module is a horizontal *service*, not a vertical stage.** Both the scraper (to extract and rate jobs) and the profiler (to assess Hyun's portfolio and answers) call into it. So the dependency graph isn't a line — it's a spine with a shared brain hanging off it.

- **Skeleton** — orchestrator. Owns the pipeline runner, the config, resume/caching/logging, and the **deterministic scoring maths** (power/geometric mean, two axes, field aggregation). It's the only place scraper data and profiler data meet.

- **Scraper** — code + its data. Per-board adapters (Wanted, Saramin, JobKorea, Notefolio), crawl/fetch, rate-limiting, and the raw cache. This is the earlier *Scraper* sub-build; its LLM-driven extraction/scoring (the *Judge*) is now just "scraper calls the LLM module".

- **Profiler** — code + Hyun's data. The v1 guided pass, later v2 (portfolio + micro-tasks + Elo), and the scoring that produces `hyun_profile`. Its data is **personal and private** — kept local, never committed, never sent to the LLM beyond what a given assessment needs.

- **LLM** — the shared brain. Model-agnostic client with retries, rate-limit, cost logging, and a response **cache**; versioned prompts and rubrics; structured-output schemas. Exposes capabilities, not a pipeline: `extract_job()`, `rate_axes()`, `assess_portfolio()`, `normalise_skill()`.
- **Outputs** (small, worth naming) — the two workbooks + the Fit/Opportunity plot. A thin reporter the skeleton drives.
## Why the LLM is horizontal
│   SKELETON   │  runner · config · deterministic scoring · reporter
│  SCRAPER  │        │  PROFILER │
│ +raw data │        │ +Hyun data│
│    LLM    │  prompts · schemas · cache · cost log  (shared service)

Scoring lives in the **skeleton**, not the LLM: the LLM produces the fuzzy 0–10 ratings, the skeleton does the deterministic arithmetic that joins them with Hyun's priors. That keeps the final scores reproducible and re-runnable without new LLM calls.
## Two design rules that make this hold up

**1. Separate code from data inside each module.** Each module gets a `data/` subfolder. Scraper data is large → git-ignored and rebuildable. Profiler data is personal → local and private. You can wipe and regenerate data without touching a line of code.
**2. Quarantine the two sources of messiness.** This is the whole reason for the split, given the tool is *both* human-calibrated *and* LLM-driven:
- The **human-calibrated, subjective, mutable** part is sealed inside the Profiler — small, hand-tunable, private.
- The **LLM's non-determinism** is sealed behind the LLM module's interface — fixed prompts, JSON schemas, temp≈0, cached and versioned.

- They only meet in the skeleton's **deterministic** scoring. So a human recalibration and an LLM prompt change can each be made and tested in isolation, without disturbing the pipeline or each other.

│   ├── scoring.py        # power/geometric mean, two axes, field aggregation
│   ├── config.yaml       # weights, p, search terms, skill aliases
│   └── contracts.py      # the seams: C1–C4 + hyun_profile schemas
│   ├── adapters/         # wanted · saramin · jobkorea · notefolio
│   └── data/             # raw_cache/ , job_urls.jsonl        (git-ignored)
│   ├── instrument/       # v1 guided pass → v2 interactive
│   └── data/             # hyun_profile.yaml , answers , portfolio refs  (private)
│   ├── client.py         # model-agnostic; retries · rate-limit · cost log · cache
│   ├── prompts/          # versioned prompts + rubrics
│   └── schemas/          # structured-output JSON schemas
└── outputs/              # jobs_ranked.xlsx · requirements_ranked.xlsx · fit_opportunity.png
Modules talk **only** through the frozen contracts, so each is testable against a fixture with the others absent:
scraper   ──C1 job_url──▶ ──C2 raw_posting──▶ llm.extract_job + llm.rate_axes
skeleton  reads C3 job_row + hyun_profile ──▶ scoring ──▶ C4 scored_row ──▶ outputs
llm       everything in/out via a JSON schema; every call cached by (prompt-hash, input-hash)

Swap the model without touching the scraper. Re-score after a weight change without re-calling the LLM. Recalibrate Hyun's profile without re-crawling. Rebuild the scrape cache without losing her data. Test any module alone. And because every LLM call is cached and every prompt versioned, calibration — which you'll iterate a lot — stays cheap and traceable.

# Execution Plan (P2) — Plan the build before building it

This is the plan for P3 (the build). Two immediate problems are solved here: **(1)** how to discover what Hyun excels at when she can't self-rate, and **(2)** how to split P3 into sub-builds that can be built and tested **separately** — scraper · judge · spreadsheet · else.

Guiding rule for the whole build: **contracts first, then a walking skeleton, then harden.** Define the data that flows between stages before writing any stage; prove the whole chain thin on ~30 jobs; only then scale each piece.
## 1. Immediate — the Profiler (discovering Hyun's strengths)

**Problem.** The Skill-alignment axis needs Hyun's strengths, but she doesn't know them, and self-report of *skill* is the least reliable signal there is. So don't ask her to rate herself in a vacuum.
**Principle.** Measure **revealed** aptitude and preference, not just stated. Keep three latent variables *separate* per field, because they diverge:
- **Interest** — what she *wants* to do
- **Aptitude** — what she's *actually good at* (revealed, not claimed)
- **Confidence** — what she *believes* she can do (used to catch blind spots — impostor gaps and over-confidence)
**Input types — deliberately not text-only** (each reveals something different):
| Input type | What it captures | Why this modality |

| **Pairwise forced-choice** ("which task/image would you rather do — or wish you'd made?") | relative preference & affinity | robust when someone has no *absolute* self-knowledge — only comparisons |

| **Visual-stimulus reactions** — show real works from each of the 10 fields, rate 1–5 on *appeal* / *"I could make this"* / *"I want to make this"* | taste vs perceived ability, per field | visual fields are judged by eye faster than by words |
| **Portfolio / artefact upload** — AI assesses her existing work | demonstrated aptitude | strongest signal; what she's *actually produced* beats any self-rating |

| **Timed micro-tasks** (arrange a layout, critique a space, storyboard 3 frames) | sampled aptitude across the reasoning styles fields reward (spatial / compositional / systems / narrative) | direct behavioural evidence |
| **Sliders** — enjoyment and *"energised vs drained"* per activity | interest + sustainability | separates "fun once" from "could do daily" |
| **Card-sort / drag-rank** of activities and the 10 fields | priorities & self-model | fast, low-friction, non-verbal |

| **Structured behavioural questions** ("what do people come to you for?", "what have you lost track of time doing?", "what do you redo until it's right?") | third-party-visible strengths | surfaces strengths others see that she discounts |

**Scoring.** Convert pairwise results to a Bradley-Terry/Elo ranking; z-score the sliders; score artefacts and micro-tasks by LLM rubric. Triangulate stated + revealed + artefact into **Interest[field]** and **Skill[field]** on 0–10, each with an **uncertainty band** from how much the signals agree. Flag every field where confidence and aptitude diverge — those blind spots are as valuable as the scores.
**Output (the contract):** the `hyun_profile` block — `Interest[]`, `Skill[]` per field + confidence — which drops straight into the scraper's `config.yaml`.
**Delivery choice for P3:** an interactive HTML artifact is the natural home (sliders, image picks, drag-rank, upload in one page). Alternative is a lighter guided session. Decide at P3 kickoff.
## 2. Contracts first — why the build is divisible

Freeze the JSONL schemas that pass between stages **before** building any stage. Once frozen, every sub-build is an isolated unit you can build and unit-test against a small **fixture file**, with none of the other stages existing yet. The four contracts:
C1  job_url      { board, job_id, url, posted_at }
C2  raw_posting  { board, job_id, url, raw_text|raw_json, fetched_at }
C3  job_row      { …schema from build spec §3…, extraction_confidence }
C4  scored_row   { job_row + fit, opportunity, final }
+   hyun_profile { interest[field], skill[field], confidence[field] }   ← from Profiler
+   skill_alias  { canonical_id: [aliases…] }                           ← config, used by Judge
Fixtures to hand-make once (they unblock parallel work): ~10 saved raw postings (for C2), ~1 list of messy skill strings (for the normaliser), ~20 scored rows (for the reporter).
- **Purpose:** discover job URLs and fetch raw detail pages; nothing else.
- **In → Out:** search config → `C1` then `C2` (raw cache on disk).
- **Contains:** per-board adapters (Wanted API, Saramin Open API, JobKorea Playwright, Notefolio), rate-limiter, resume/`seen` set.
- **Isolated test:** run one board, one search term, assert ≥N cached postings and valid `C2` records. No LLM, no scoring involved.
- **Done:** all four boards yield valid `C2`; re-run fetches only new ids.
### B. Judge  *(the AI overseer)*
- **Purpose:** turn raw postings into structured, scored rows.
- **In → Out:** `C2` + `skill_alias` + `hyun_profile` → `C3` then `C4`.
- **Contains:** (i) LLM structured-extraction to the schema, (ii) the **Normaliser** call (see D), (iii) the scorer (weighted geometric / power mean, two axes, ε-floor).
- **Isolated test:** run against the 10-posting **fixture** — the Scraper need not exist yet. Assert stable scores at temp≈0 and that hand-checked rows match.
- **Done:** fixture rows extract correctly, scores reproduce run-to-run, calibration against Hyun's hand-scores passes tolerance.
- **Purpose:** turn scored rows into deliverables.
- **In → Out:** `C4` → `jobs_ranked.xlsx` (+ `field_ranked` tab), `requirements_ranked.xlsx`, and the Fit-vs-Opportunity scatter.
- **Isolated test:** run against the 20-row fixture; open the files, check sorting, tabs, the field-aggregation formula and the plot. No scraper or judge needed.
- **Done:** both workbooks generate from fixture and from real `C4` identically.
### D. Else  *(shared + glue)*

- **Normaliser:** `skill_alias` dictionary + embedding/LLM fallback that logs new merges for approval. Feeds the Judge. *Test:* messy-strings fixture → correct canonical ids; unknown term is logged, not silently merged.
- **Profiler:** section 1 above. Independent of the scraping chain; produces `hyun_profile`.
- **Orchestrator + config:** `config.yaml` (search terms, weights, `p`, aliases), the stage runner, caching, logging, the resume logic. Built **last**, once the stages it glues are done.
## 4. Build order & parallelism
Step 0  Freeze contracts C1–C4 + profile/alias         (unblocks everything)
Step 1  BUILD IN PARALLEL against fixtures:
Profiler  |  Scraper  |  Judge(fixture)  |  Normaliser  |  Reporter(fixture)
Step 2  WALKING SKELETON — wire a thin path end-to-end on ~30 real jobs
Scraper(30) → Judge → Reporter,  Profiler run with Hyun
>>> CALIBRATION GATE: LLM scores track Hyun's hand-scores + rankings sane?
NO  → fix rubric/weights, do not scale
Step 3  HARDEN — scale each sub-build to full volume, add the other boards
Step 4  Orchestrator — glue into one resumable overnight run

Two independent roots (**Profiler** and **Scraper**) can start at once. **Judge** and **Reporter** don't wait for the Scraper — they build against fixtures, thanks to the frozen contracts. This is what makes "build them separately" real rather than aspirational.
## 5. Definition of done per sub-build
| Sub-build | Done when… |
| Scraper | 4 boards → valid `C2`; incremental re-run works |
| Judge | fixture extracts + scores reproducibly; passes calibration gate |
| Spreadsheet | both workbooks + plot generate from fixture and real data |
| Else — Normaliser | fixture maps correctly; unknowns logged for review |
| Else — Profiler | produces `hyun_profile` with uncertainty + blind-spot flags |
| Else — Orchestrator | one command runs the resumable end-to-end overnight job |

Order I'd take: **Profiler first** (Hyun's inputs gate calibration and take real time to gather) and **contracts + a one-board Scraper slice** in parallel, converging on the Step-2 walking skeleton. Open choices for kickoff: Profiler delivery (interactive artifact vs guided session), and which board the Scraper slice targets first (Wanted is cleanest).
# Korea Job Scraper — Build Specification

**Goal:** collect design/spatial/3D job postings from Korean boards, score each one, and aggregate to help Hyun decide **which field** to pursue. Output: two spreadsheets — ranked jobs, and ranked requirements.
- **Target boards:** Wanted, Saramin, JobKorea, Notefolio.

- **Hyun is a Korean national / F-visa holder** → no visa-sponsorship filter. Korean-language postings are fully viable, so keep Korean text and score it directly (translation optional, only for your own readability).
- `koreajobs.com` is a parked domain for sale — ignore it entirely.

**Careers under comparison:** UX/UI Designer · Spatial/VMD Designer · Exhibition Designer · Brand Space Designer · Architectural Visualization Artist (ArchViz) · 3D Generalist · Environment Artist · XR/Spatial Experience Designer · Technical Artist · Motion/Graphic Designer.
## 1. Architecture — staged and resumable
Do **not** score live during the crawl. Four decoupled, idempotent stages, each writing to disk so a crash resumes without re-fetching:
[1 discover]  listing pages  → job_urls.jsonl        (id, board, url, posted_at)
[2 fetch]     each detail    → raw_cache/{board}/{id}.json  (raw JSON or HTML)
[3 extract]   LLM pass       → jobs.jsonl             (structured row + confidence)
[4 score]     pure functions → jobs_scored.jsonl → two .xlsx files

Rules: a `seen` set keyed by `board:id` so re-runs skip cached items; rate-limit ~1 request / 1–2 s per board; realistic user-agent; retry with backoff. robots.txt permits crawling, but keep it personal-use and gentle — several boards' terms restrict scraping even where robots allows.
## 2. Extraction per board (API-first)

Modern boards are JavaScript SPAs — never regex the rendered HTML. In each case, open the site, filter the browser **Network tab to XHR/Fetch**, and copy the JSON call the page makes. Hit that endpoint directly. Fall back to Playwright only where no clean JSON exists.

- **Wanted (wanted.co.kr)** — exposes a JSON API (look for `api.wanted.co.kr`). Typically a list endpoint (paged by category/tag + offset) and a detail endpoint per job id. Design category is filterable. This is the cleanest of the four — start here to prove the pipeline end-to-end.

- **Saramin (saramin.co.kr)** — has an **official recruitment Open API** (`oapi.saramin.co.kr`, free key). Prefer it over scraping: structured, ToS-clean, keyword + job-category filters. Fall back to page JSON if the key's coverage is thin.
- **JobKorea (jobkorea.co.kr)** — no public API. SPA/HTML → use **Playwright** to render listing + detail pages, then parse the JSON embedded in the page state where present.
- **Notefolio (노트폴리오)** — SPA with internal JSON endpoints; design-native so best for VMD/graphic/spatial. Verify endpoints in the Network tab; Playwright fallback.
**Search seeds** (run each board's search with both English and Korean terms): UX/UI, 3D, VMD/비주얼머천다이징, 공간디자인, 전시디자인, 브랜드공간, 건축시각화/ArchViz, 모션그래픽, 테크니컬아티스트, XR/AR/VR, 환경아트/environment artist.
**Entry-level flag** — match Korean tokens, not English: `신입` (entry) / `경력무관` (experience irrelevant) / `인턴` (intern) vs `경력` (experienced).
## 3. Job row schema (stage 3 output)
Extract with a single LLM call per cached posting, returning a fixed JSON schema. Never hand-parse free text.
| board, job_id, url, posted_at, scraped_at | provenance |
| job_title, company | raw |
| mapped_career | best match from the 10 careers above (or `other`) |
| entry_level | Yes/No (from token match, LLM confirms) |
| required_software | list of **canonical** tool ids (see §4) |
| visualization_score, spatial_relevance, cs_usefulness, english_usefulness, freelance_potential, market_demand, barrier_to_entry | 0–10 each, LLM-rated with a short rubric in the prompt |
| why_it_fits | 1–2 sentence LLM summary |
| skills_to_learn | tools/skills demanded that Hyun lacks |
| extraction_confidence | 0–1 — lets you filter low-quality parses |
| dedup_key | normalised `company + title` for cross-board dedup |

Pin the LLM to **structured output / JSON schema** and a **temperature near 0** so scores are stable and comparable across postings. Put the rubric for each 0–10 axis in the system prompt (e.g. "spatial_relevance: 10 = core spatial/VMD/exhibition work; 0 = no physical-space component").
## 4. Requirement normalisation (the synonym problem)

Maintain a canonical skill catalogue; map every raw mention (English **and** Korean) to one id before counting. Rule-based alias dictionary first; for unseen terms, fall back to embedding/LLM matching and **log new merges to a review file** you approve, so the catalogue improves without silently mis-merging.
Seed dictionary (extend as you go):
unreal:     [Unreal, Unreal Engine, UE5, UE4, 언리얼]
Then **+1 per canonical hit** across all postings → frequency table = **portfolio priority** (most-demanded tools first). Weight by `mapped_career` if you want per-field portfolio advice.
## 5. Scoring — weighted geometric mean, two axes

Raw multiplication over-punishes and collapses to near-zero with no spread. Instead: normalise each sub-score to 0–1, **invert the barrier** (`accessibility = 1 − barrier/10`), then take a weighted geometric mean with a small floor `ε` so a single weak factor hurts but doesn't zero the row.
geo(scores, weights) = exp( Σ wᵢ · ln(max(sᵢ, ε)) ),   Σwᵢ = 1,   ε ≈ 0.05
Fit         = geo(interest, skill_alignment, visualization, spatial_relevance)
Final       = 100 · (0.6·Fit + 0.4·Opportunity)

`interest` and `skill_alignment` are Hyun's own 0–10 ratings per career (constant within a field), the rest come from the posting. Keep all weights in a `config.yaml` and **run a sensitivity check**: does the field ranking survive ±20 % weight changes? If not, the winner isn't robust.

Also plot **Fit vs Opportunity** as a 2D scatter — it answers "which field" far better than one number (high-fit/high-opportunity is the sweet spot; high-fit/low-opportunity is a passion-but-thin-market warning).
**Field-level aggregation (the actual decision):** don't let one great posting crown a field.
field_score(career) = median(top-10 Fit of that career's jobs)
The `log` term rewards fields with real entry-level volume (demand for someone starting out) without letting a flood of postings dominate.

1. **`jobs_ranked.xlsx`** — one row per posting, sorted by Final; columns from §3 plus Fit, Opportunity, Final. Add a second tab: `field_ranked` (career, field_score, #jobs, #entry-level, median Fit).
2. **`requirements_ranked.xlsx`** — canonical skill, frequency, % of postings, and top fields demanding it. This is Hyun's portfolio to-do list.

Because stages are cached and resumable, "leave it overnight" = run stages 1–2 (network-bound, slow due to rate-limiting) first, then 3–4 (LLM-bound). Batch stage 3 and cap concurrency to respect model rate limits. Log every skip/retry. A second run next day only fetches *new* postings.

# Meta-Plan — How to run the "which field for Hyun" decision
This sits *above* the build spec. The scraper is one instrument; this document is how to run the whole decision so the answer is trustworthy and Hyun actually acts on it.
## The one principle everything else serves

**Decision-first, not data-first.** The output is not a spreadsheet — it is a field Hyun commits to and can enter. Every planning choice is judged by "does this make the *decision* better and more defensible," not "does this produce more data." A beautiful 10,000-row scored sheet that doesn't change or justify the choice is wasted effort.

1. **De-risk the biggest assumption first.** The riskiest belief here is *"the formula + LLM scoring discriminates between fields in a way that matches reality."* If that's false, the overnight machine produces confident nonsense. So test it on ~30 jobs before building anything expensive (see Phase 1). Cheapest experiment first.

2. **Human priors before machine runs.** Two of the scoring axes — Interest and Skill alignment — are *Hyun's* inputs, not the scraper's. The market half is worthless without her half. Elicit her ratings, weights and constraints up front, or the whole score is garbage-in.

3. **Pre-register, then run.** Lock the weights and rubric in `config.yaml` *before* seeing results. Otherwise it's too easy to tune weights until the tool "confirms" the field she already wanted. If she does change weights later, do it in the open and re-report.

4. **Treat scores as ordinal, not exact.** "87.3" rests on soft 0–10 guesses. Rank and band into tiers (A/B/C); never defend a decision on a 2-point gap. The number informs judgement; it doesn't replace it.
5. **The AI scores; the human decides.** The overseer extracts and rates. Hyun is the sole arbiter of the final call. Guard against automation bias — a high number is an argument, not a verdict.
6. **Time-box it.** Set a "decide by" date now. This exists to *end* deliberation, not to feed it. Analysis paralysis is the most likely failure of a project this well-resourced.
## Phased plan with go/no-go gates
**Phase 0 — Decision design** *(before any code)*

Define what makes a field "right": Hyun's constraints (location, salary floor, employment vs freelance, timeline, risk tolerance), her 0–10 Interest and Skill self-ratings for each of the 10 careers, and the axis weights. Agree what "good enough to decide" looks like.
→ *Artefact:* one-page decision brief + filled `config.yaml`.
→ **Gate:** don't build until Hyun's priors and weights exist.
**Phase 1 — Calibration recon** *(cheap, manual/sampled)*

Pull ~20–30 real postings per field by hand or a throwaway script. Hyun scores a subset by hand; compare against the LLM's scores on the same postings. Check three things: (a) the boards actually have volume in these fields, (b) the axes discriminate (not everything scores 7/10), (c) the ranking passes the sniff test on obvious cases. Tune the rubric and the power-mean `p` against this gold set.
→ *Artefact:* calibration set + agreement notes + tuned rubric.

→ **Gate (the important one):** proceed to the full build *only if* LLM scores track Hyun's within tolerance and the ranking looks sane. If not, fix the rubric/formula — do **not** run overnight on a broken scorer.
**Phase 2 — Build & full run**
Execute the build spec: crawl → cache → extract → score → two spreadsheets. Leave overnight.
**Phase 3 — Interpret & stress-test** *(not "highest number wins")*

Read the **Fit vs Opportunity** 2D map, not just the sorted list. Run the ±20 % weight sensitivity check — does the top field survive? Cross-check the top 2–3 fields against Hyun's gut: agreement is confidence, disagreement is the most valuable signal in the whole project and must be understood, not overridden.
→ *Artefact:* short decision memo — top fields, why, robustness, and where number and intuition diverge.
**Phase 4 — Commit & act**

Pick the field. Derive the portfolio plan directly from `requirements_ranked.xlsx` (most-demanded tools she lacks = build these first). Set a 4–6 week review checkpoint to confirm the choice still feels right once she starts building toward it.
→ *Artefact:* chosen field + ranked portfolio/skills roadmap + review date.
| Garbage-in scoring (bad/inconsistent rubric) | Phase 1 calibration against Hyun's hand-scores; temp≈0; rubric per axis |
| False precision (trusting decimals) | Band into tiers; decisions never rest on <5-point gaps |
| Confirmation bias (tuning weights to a wanted answer) | Pre-register weights before results; changes made transparently |
| Automation bias (number overrides judgement) | Human is decider; treat divergence as signal, not error |
| Scrape-ability ≠ opportunity (boards over/under-represent fields) | Don't let a thin scrape kill a field; note freelance/agency/overseas channels the boards miss |
| Analysis paralysis | Time-box + "decide by" date set in Phase 0 |
- **You (the build/analysis):** boards, pipeline, scoring, spreadsheets, sensitivity checks.
- **Hyun (the decider):** priors, weights, calibration hand-scores, final call.
- **The AI overseer:** extraction and rating only — it never decides.

We can decide when: Hyun's priors are set, the scorer is calibrated and its top-tier fields are robust to ±20 % weight changes, and the memo explains *why* the leading field wins in plain language. If a plain-language "why" doesn't exist, the model isn't ready — keep iterating, don't ship the number.

## Section D — What others see  *(third-party aptitude — often the truest signal)*
1. What do people **come to you** for help with?
2. What have you **lost track of time** doing?
3. What do you **redo until it's right** even when no one asked?
4. What have you been **praised or paid** for?
5. What do you **pick up faster** than people around you?
## Section E — Proof of work  *(revealed aptitude — rough now, assessed properly in stage 2)*
List up to 5 things you've made and are a bit proud of. For each: what it was, **what *you* specifically did**, and which field (F1–F10) it's closest to.
## Section F — Curiosity rank  *(self-model)*
Rank all ten fields F1–F10 from *most* to *least* curious-to-try. Gut order, 20 seconds.
Deliberately simple for v1 (the real weighting waits for stage 2).
`Interest = 10 × ( 0.5·norm(enjoy) + 0.3·norm(energy) + 0.2·rank_score )`, then **+1** per forced-choice win for that field (cap 10). `norm(x)=(x−1)/4`; `rank_score` = (10 − rank + 1)/10.
**Skill[field] (0–10) — weight *evidence* over self-claim:**
`Skill = 10 × ( 0.25·(C/3) + 0.45·evidence_D + 0.30·evidence_E )`

where `evidence_D`/`evidence_E` ∈ {0, 0.5, 1} = how directly sections D and E point at that field (none / indirect / direct). If a field has **only** a Section-C number and no D/E evidence, cap Skill at 5 and mark it low-confidence.
**Confidence[field]:** the raw Section-C value (0–3) → {0, 0.33, 0.67, 1}.

**Blind-spot flag:** raise it where **Confidence is low but D/E evidence is strong** (she undersells a real strength) or **Confidence is high but no evidence** (over-confidence). These flags are an output in their own right — they tell us where the numbers are least trustworthy.
**Uncertainty:** mark **all** Skill priors high-uncertainty in v1. Stage 2 (portfolio assessment + micro-tasks + Elo on the pairwise) is what tightens them.

The maths is deliberately simple and deterministic — no model calls. It follows
Profiler_v1_Guided_Pass.md, "Scoring key -> hyun_profile", to the letter:
Interest = 10 * ( 0.5*norm(enjoy) + 0.3*norm(energy) + 0.2*rank_score )
then +1 per forced-choice win for that field, capped at 10.
norm(x) = (x-1)/4 ;  rank_score = (10 - rank + 1)/10.
Skill[field] (0-10) — weight evidence over self-claim:
Skill = 10 * ( 0.25*(C/3) + 0.45*evidence_D + 0.30*evidence_E )
evidence_D / evidence_E in {0, 0.5, 1} = how directly D / E point at it.
If a field has ONLY a Section-C number and no D/E evidence, cap Skill at 5
Confidence[field]: raw Section-C value 0..3 -> {0, 0.33, 0.67, 1}.
Blind-spot flag: raised where Confidence is low but D/E evidence is strong
(undersells a real strength), or Confidence is high but there is no evidence
Uncertainty: ALL skill priors are high-uncertainty in v1.

scraper/test_scraper.py — standalone self-test for the SCRAPER module.
Runs discover + fetch over the hand-made fixtures (no network) and asserts:
* every discovered record is a valid C1 JobUrl and round-trips via contracts
* job_urls.jsonl is real JSONL of C1 records
* every fetched record is a valid C2 RawPosting (raw_json or raw_text set)
and round-trips off disk via contracts
* the resume/seen set (keyed board:job_id) skips already-seen ids on re-run
* non-design postings (backend eng, accounting, sales) are filtered out
Run:  python scraper/test_scraper.py      (from the repo root)
Exits non-zero on failure; prints a summary on success.
from contracts import JobUrl, RawPosting, from_dict, read_jsonl, to_dict  # noqa: E402
from scraper import crawl  # noqa: E402
from scraper.adapters.jobkorea import (  # noqa: E402
# Deliberately-excluded noise in the fixtures (non-design postings):
# The self-test is OFFLINE and adapter-complete: pin all four boards and
# fixture mode, regardless of the runtime config (which may be live and
# narrowed to a subset of boards, e.g. Phase-1 = wanted only).
cfg["boards"]["enabled"] = ["wanted", "saramin", "jobkorea", "notefolio"]
keys = {u.key for u in new}
assert keys == EXPECTED_KEYS, f"discover keys mismatch: {keys ^ EXPECTED_KEYS}"
assert not (keys & EXCLUDED_KEYS), "non-design postings leaked into discover"
# each is a valid C1 and round-trips through contracts
assert u.board and u.job_id and u.url
assert from_dict(JobUrl, to_dict(u)) == u, f"C1 round-trip failed for {u.key}"
# job_urls.jsonl is real JSONL of C1 records
assert all(isinstance(r, JobUrl) for r in on_disk)
assert {r.key for r in on_disk} == EXPECTED_KEYS
# resume: a second discover discovers nothing new
assert again == [], f"resume should skip seen urls, got {[u.key for u in again]}"
fetched = crawl.fetch(cfg, urls_path=urls_path, cache_dir=cache_dir, sleep=0)
fkeys = {r.key for r in fetched}
assert fkeys == EXPECTED_KEYS, f"fetch keys mismatch: {fkeys ^ EXPECTED_KEYS}"
assert r.board and r.job_id and r.url and r.fetched_at

assert from_dict(RawPosting, to_dict(r)) == r, f"C2 round-trip failed for {r.key}"

assert by_key["jobkorea:45872301"].raw_text, "jobkorea should carry raw_text (HTML)"
assert by_key["wanted:210031"].raw_json, "wanted should carry raw_json (API)"

again_f = crawl.fetch(cfg, urls_path=urls_path, cache_dir=cache_dir, sleep=0)
assert again_f == [], f"resume should skip cached postings, got {[r.key for r in again_f]}"

print(f"  fetch    : {len(fetched)} C2 RawPosting records (round-trip OK, resume OK)")

# Agent protocol — MANDATORY for every module build
You are building ONE module in a shared tree. Obey all of this; the gate enforces it.
## graphify enforcement (has teeth — not optional)
Before any work, and at every milestone, use the gate:
gate = open_gate(".", strict=True)          # repo root; real graphify, fail-closed
gate.read("<module>")                        # 1. READ the graph BEFORE you build
# ...build a milestone's worth of code...
gate.checkpoint("<module>", "<milestone>",   # 2. WRITE at each milestone
gate.assert_complete("<module>")             # 3. module is DONE only if this passes
- `checkpoint()` before `read()` → refused. Read first.
- Only the milestones declared for your module in `graph_gate.MILESTONES` are accepted.
- Your module is NOT done until `assert_complete()` + `verify()` pass. Don't report done otherwise.
- Run bash with `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` so `graphify` resolves (the gate also finds it in ~/.local/bin).
- graphify writes locally only. NEVER run `graphify label` / clustering (those call a model). Use only `graphify update . --no-cluster` (the gate already does this).
- Never send `profiler/data/` or `scraper/data/` anywhere. Keep personal data local.
- Talk to other modules ONLY through `skeleton/contracts.py`. Do not import another module's internals.
- Read config from `skeleton/config.yaml` (it's a STUB — don't hardcode; read values).
- Build against small fixtures so your module is testable ALONE, without the others.
- Keep deps light; prefer stdlib. Write a runnable self-test and show it passing.
- Put your code in your module's folder and its data in `<module>/data/`.

skeleton/contracts.py — the frozen seams between modules.
These dataclasses ARE the interface. Modules (scraper, profiler, llm, reporter)
talk to each other only through these shapes, so each can be built and tested
against a fixture with the others absent.
Rule: treat these as stable. If a field must change, bump CONTRACT_VERSION and
update every module + fixture in the same change. Don't quietly reshape.
Stdlib only — no third-party deps, so any module can import it freely.
from typing import Any, Iterable, Iterator, Optional
CONTRACT_VERSION = "0.2.0"  # 0.2.0: +JobRow.remote_flag, +JobRow.site_intensity (lifestyle wiring)
# The ten careers under comparison. Keys are canonical and must match the
# hyun_profile keys in config.yaml exactly.
# C1 — a discovered job URL (scraper: discover stage)
board: str            # "wanted" | "saramin" | "jobkorea" | "notefolio"
job_id: str           # board-local id; unique within a board
posted_at: Optional[str] = None   # ISO date if the listing exposes one
# C2 — a raw fetched posting (scraper: fetch stage → raw cache)
raw_text: Optional[str] = None        # for HTML-scraped boards
raw_json: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None   # for API/JSON boards
# C3 — a structured, extracted job row (llm.extract_job + llm.rate_axes)
# Axis ratings are Optional so an un-scored row is representable.
mapped_career: str = "other"          # one of CAREERS, or "other"
required_software: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # canonical ids

The rule is not a suggestion. Every module MUST:
1. read()        the knowledge graph before it does any work   (context in)
2. checkpoint()  at each required milestone                     (write out)
and a module's output is REJECTED unless every one of its milestones has been
checkpointed. assert_complete() raises; the orchestrator refuses the module.
What gives it teeth (each is enforced in code, not documented as etiquette):
T1  checkpoint() before read()            -> raises  (no blind writes)
T2  checkpoint() of an unknown milestone  -> raises  (no off-book milestones)
T3  assert_complete() with any gap        -> raises  (module cannot be 'done')
T4  verify() detects a tampered/forged ledger via per-artifact content hashes
T5  strict backend fail-closed: if graphify is required but absent -> raises
T6  a file lock serialises graph writes so parallel agents can't corrupt it
Privacy: the graph build NEVER ingests personal data. IGNORED_PATHS (Hyun's
profiler data, the raw scrape cache) are excluded from what graphify sees,
because graphify sends semantic content to an upstream model.

Five stages, each idempotent and cached to disk so a crash resumes without

discover → fetch → extract → score → report
[discover] search config → job_urls.jsonl        (C1, keyed board:id)

need the scraper, extract needs the llm module — each is behind an import
guard, so on a skeleton-only checkout the runner still scores + reports from
a fixture (or from whatever jobs.jsonl already exists).
